text:
The pedestrian will likely prevail on a claim for fraudulent misrepresentation because the adjuster knowingly made a false statement of law (that the pedestrian was not entitled to compensation) with the intent to induce reliance, and the pedestrian’s rejection of the offer and subsequent litigation show reliance and damages. However, if the jurisdiction treats misrepresentations of law as non-actionable absent a special relationship, the pedestrian may need to show the adjuster had superior knowledge or a fiduciary duty.  
CONFIDENCE: 85
